subject: economics

moments.title: The Wall Street Crash
moments.who: Investors and the New York Stock Exchange
moments.body: On 24 October ('Black Thursday') and 29 October ('Black Tuesday') 1929, US stock prices crashed. The Dow lost almost 90% of its value by 1932. US unemployment hit 25%. The Great Depression spread globally. Classical economics, with its faith in self-correcting markets, had no convincing response.
moments.takeaway: The intellectual crisis was as severe as the economic one. The discipline needed a new framework.

moments.title: The General Theory
moments.body: Keynes's 'The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money' argues that aggregate demand drives output, that economies can be stuck at high-unemployment equilibrium, and that government spending can shift them. The 'multiplier' makes fiscal policy potent. Saving is not automatically investment; liquidity preference matters.

quote.text: In the long run we are all dead.
quote.attrib: Keynes, A Tract on Monetary Reform, 1923

moments.takeaway: Keynes shifted economics from a primarily microeconomic, equilibrium-based discipline to one with a distinct macroeconomic theory of slumps and policy.

moments.title: Bretton Woods
moments.who: Keynes, Harry Dexter White, and delegates from 44 nations
moments.body: At Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, the postwar international monetary system is designed. The dollar is pegged to gold, other currencies to the dollar. The IMF and the World Bank are founded. Keynes's proposal for a global currency (the 'bancor') was rejected; White's dollar-centred system won.
moments.takeaway: Bretton Woods underpinned 25 years of postwar growth ('les trente glorieuses'). It collapsed in 1971 when Nixon ended dollar-gold convertibility.

now.title: Keynes after Keynes
now.body: Monetarism (Friedman) and New Classical economics (Lucas) eclipsed Keynesianism from the late 1970s, partly in response to the failure of crude Keynesian models in the stagflation of the 1970s. The 2008 crisis brought a Keynesian revival — Paul Krugman, Olivier Blanchard, Mark Carney all explicitly invoked Keynes. Modern Monetary Theory (MMT) has roots in chartalist Keynesianism.
now.open_questions: Was the 2008-21 era proof Keynes was right, or did near-zero interest rates expose the limits of monetary policy and the need for new frameworks? The post-COVID inflation revived doubts about loose fiscal policy.

reflection: Keynes thought economics should serve civilisation, not constrain it. The 'Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren' (1930) essay imagined that by 2030 the economic problem would be solved and we'd worry about the use of leisure. It hasn't worked out that way — but the question is still live.
